title: U.S. House · California's 2nd District
area: Spans the North Coast of California from the Golden Gate Bridge north to the Oregon border, following the 2025 Proposition 50 mid-decade redistricting.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, approved by voters on November 4, 2025, which redrew the state's congressional map.

In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, Jared Huffman (D) placed first with 56.5% (139,662 votes) and Robin Littau (R) placed second with 11.4% (28,222 votes) out of 247,293 total votes cast; both advanced to the general election.

candidates.name: Jared Huffman
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2 top-two primary outright with a majority of votes cast
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for California's 2nd District (since 2013); Ranking Member, House Natural Resources Committee

priorities.text: Names affordability as a top priority, citing tariffs, trade wars and tax policy as drivers of rising costs for groceries, energy, healthcare and housing.
priorities.quote: Affordability - we have an affordability crisis in America, and Trump's tariffs, trade wars, actual wars, and massive tax giveaways to billionaires have caused everyday costs to skyrocket. We must put working families first and make lowering costs -- for groceries, energy and utility bills, healthcare, housing and more -- the top priority.

priorities.text: Says he will push for restored congressional oversight of the executive branch and a ban on stock trading by members of Congress, the President, and other executive branch officials.
priorities.quote: I will fight to hold Trump and others in the administration accountable by restoring serious oversight and investigations in a Democratic majority next Congress. I will also demand a total ban on stock trading (including prediction markets) by members of Congress along with the President and other executive branch officials.

positions.summary: Opposes broad tariffs, citing them as a cause of rising consumer costs.
positions.quote: Trump's tariffs, trade wars, actual wars, and massive tax giveaways to billionaires have caused everyday costs to skyrocket.

positions.summary: States he is an original cosponsor of the Green New Deal resolution and describes the Inflation Reduction Act as the most ambitious climate and clean energy legislation in U.S. history.
positions.quote: As a climate leader and an original cosponsor of the Green New Deal resolution, these priorities are front and center in all my work for California’s Second District.

positions.summary: Lists raising the minimum wage among the measures that can help working families.
positions.quote: keeping health care affordable, making sure more workers have equal protections, raising the minimum wage, and providing paid family leave and child care

record.text: Elected by House Democrats as Ranking Member of the Committee on Natural Resources for the 2025-2026 session.
Serves on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, including the Highways and Transit and Water Resources and Environment subcommittees, for the 2025-2026 session.

candidates.name: Robin Littau
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary
candidates.currentRole: Board member, Enterprise Elementary School District (Redding, CA)

priorities.text: Lists reducing taxation and burdensome legislation, restoring government integrity and transparency, and pursuing accountability for political waste and fraud as her main campaign messages.
priorities.quote: I want to create, replace, revise and approve common sense legislation that BENEFITS Americans and BUILDS America, by decreasing burdensome taxation and hindering legislation. Integrity filled leaders are essential for all leadership positions.

candidates.researchNotes: Her 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey names parental rights, public safety and reducing taxes and waste as themes but does not address the guide's issues. At the Apr. 2, 2026 League of Women Voters forum in Redding (Jefferson Public Radio), her quoted remark was general. No campaign website located. No positions or statements added.

researchNotes: Robin Littau has no prior officeholder record beyond her local school board seat, so no additional record items beyond that background are documented. Biography gaps: Huffman's House 'About' page could not be retrieved, so his biography draws on Ballotpedia (including his own survey response) and Wikipedia; Littau's biography rests on her Ballotpedia survey response alone and has not been independently verified.
